questions.question: The Upper House of a State Legislature is known as the ____________.
questions.solution:
The Upper House of a State Legislature is known as the Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council).
  • Permanent Body: Like the Rajya Sabha, it is not subject to dissolution.
  • Vidhan Sabha: This is the Lower House (Legislative Assembly), which is the direct representative body of the people.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India comprises the Chief Justice and not more than ______ other Judges appointed by the President of India.
questions.solution:
The Supreme Court currently comprises the Chief Justice and 33 other Judges (Total strength of 34).
  • Appointment: Every judge is appointed by the President.
  • Expansion: The Parliament has the power to increase the number of judges; the current strength was settled in 2019.

questions.question: The oath of office to the Vice-President is administered by the ________.
questions.solution:
The President of India (or someone appointed by them) administers the oath of office to the Vice-President.
  • Article 69: This article explicitly mentions the President as the authority for the Vice-Presidential oath.

questions.question: Who among the following was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution:
Gulzarilal Nanda was the shortest-serving Prime Minister, having served as acting PM for 13 days twice.
  • Note: Among elected PMs, Atal Bihari Vajpayee had a famous 13-day stint in 1996, but Nanda holds the record for the absolute shortest durations.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Election Commission of India founded?
questions.solution:
The Election Commission of India was founded on 25th January 1950.
  • National Voters' Day: To mark this foundation, January 25 is celebrated annually as National Voters' Day.

questions.question: What is the tenure of office for the Chief Election Commissioner?
questions.option_1: 6 years or up to the age of 60 years
questions.option_2: 5 years or up to the age of 65 years
questions.option_3: 6 years or up to the age of 65 years
questions.option_4: 5 years or up to the age of 60 years
questions.solution:
The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) holds office for a tenure of 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
  • Independence: The CEC has the same status and removal process as a judge of the Supreme Court to ensure impartiality.

questions.question: The organisation that Comptroller and Auditor General heads is known as ___________.
questions.option_4: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
questions.solution:
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.
  • Guardian: The CAG is the external auditor for the government and ensures financial accountability of the executive to the legislature.

questions.question: In the state legislative assembly, the Money bill can be introduced with the prior permission of __________.
questions.solution:
In the State Legislative Assembly, a Money Bill can only be introduced with the prior permission of the Governor.
  • Exclusion: Just like the Centre (where the President's recommendation is needed), a Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Legislative Council (Upper House).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty of the Indian citizens?
questions.option_2: To cherish and follow the noble ideas that inspired our national struggle for freedom.
questions.option_3: To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
questions.option_4: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
questions.solution:
Mandatory national service is not a Fundamental Duty.
  • Clarification: While Article 51A(d) asks citizens to 'render national service when called upon to do so', there is no mandatory 5-year requirement prescribed.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT a member of the National Human Rights Commission?
questions.option_1: Former Judge of the Supreme Court
questions.option_2: Former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
questions.option_3: Former Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.solution:
A District Magistrate is not a member of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC).
  • Composition: The NHRC consists of a Chairperson (former CJI or SC Judge), a former SC Judge, a former HC Chief Justice, and members with expertise in human rights.

questions.question: A student, on his school assignment, is taking a session on how to make compost at home for using it at a park. Which fundamental duty is he performing?
questions.option_1: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
questions.option_2: To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
questions.option_3: To protect and improve the natural environment
questions.option_4: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry
questions.solution:
A student teaching composting is performing the duty to protect and improve the natural environment (Article 51A[g]).
  • Scope: This duty specifically includes the protection of forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and having compassion for living creatures.

questions.question: Which fundamental duty applies on you when you see a few school students, on their educational trip to Humayun’s tomb, writing their names on the walls?
questions.option_1: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
questions.option_2: To protect and improve the natural environment
questions.option_4: To defend the country and render national service
questions.solution:
Preventing students from defacing a tomb relates to the duty to safeguard public property (Article 51A[i]).
  • Context: Public property includes historical monuments and government buildings; the duty also mandates abjuring violence.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?
questions.option_1: To prohibit trade in rare and endangered species
questions.option_2: To value and preserve rich heritage of the country's composite culture
questions.option_3: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
questions.option_4: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
questions.solution:
Prohibiting trade in rare species is not a Fundamental Duty.
  • Legal distinction: While it is part of the Wildlife Protection Act and a DPSP (Article 48A), it is not one of the 11 duties listed under 51A.

questions.question: Which Committee identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The Justice Verma Committee (1999) identified legal provisions already in place for the implementation of some Fundamental Duties.
  • Findings: For example, the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act implements the duty to respect the Flag and Anthem.

questions.question: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 deals with subsistence allowance in which of the following Sections?
questions.solution:
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 provides for subsistence allowance in Section 5.
  • Provision: It entitles a married Muslim woman upon whom talaq is pronounced to receive a subsistence allowance from her husband for herself and her dependent children.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.option_1: They aim at establishing social and economic democracy in the country.
questions.option_2: They are positive, as they require the State to do certain things.
questions.option_3: These have moral and political sanctions.
questions.option_4: They promote welfare of individuals. Hence, they are personal and individualistic.
questions.solution:
The statement that 'DPSPs promote welfare of individuals and are personal/individualistic' is INCORRECT.
  • Socialist Focus: DPSPs are socialistic and collective in nature, aiming to establish social and economic democracy for the community as a whole. Fundamental Rights are the ones considered individualistic.

questions.question: Which writ is issued by a high court or supreme court when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
questions.solution:
The writ of Prohibition is issued by a higher court to a lower court to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction.
  • Prevention vs. Cure: Prohibition is issued while the case is pending (preventative), while Certiorari is issued after the order is passed to quash it (curative).

questions.question: The number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall NOT be less than _______.
questions.solution:
The number of ministers in a state, including the CM, shall not be less than 12.
  • Maximum Limit: It also cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly (91st Amendment Act, 2003).

questions.question: The ________ of every state unfurls the flag in its capital on the Republic Day.
questions.solution:
The Governor of every state unfurls the flag in the state capital on Republic Day.
  • Protocol: On Independence Day, the Chief Minister performs the flag hoisting, mirroring the President/PM relationship at the Centre.

questions.question: The concept of Public Interest Litigation originated in _______________.
questions.solution:
The concept of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) originated in the USA in the mid-1960s.
  • India: It was introduced in India in the late 1970s and 1980s by Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer.

questions.question: Who is considered the highest law officer of the state in India?
questions.solution:
The Advocate General is the highest law officer of a state.
  • Article 165: They are appointed by the Governor and perform similar duties for the State government as the Attorney General does for the Union.
